newsitem.title: UK: Millwall in talks with bankers NatWest.
newsitem.headline: Millwall in talks with bankers NatWest.

text.p: Millwall Holdings Plc, owners of English second division soccer club Millwall FC, were on Tuesday holding urgent talks about their financial situation, bankers NatWest said in a statement.

"We understand shares in Millwall Holdings Plc were suspended at 1045 GMT after discussions with their own financial advisers with whom we believe Millwall are still continuing their discussions," NatWest said in a statement.
"There has been previous dialogue with NatWest about Millwall's financial position and this will continue," it added.
The shares, valued at 4p each, were suspended on Tuesday.
NatWest, believed to be the main bankers to the company, did not reveal how much it had loaned to the club.
The company's accounts for the year to May 31, 1996 showed it had gross borrowings of almost 10 million pounds.
The company made a pre-tax loss of 2.9 million stg in the period, a spell in which the soccer club was relegated.
Millwall said it raised 2.45 million pounds in player sales in the first six weeks of the current financial year.
